title: DA-CASE: reusable measurements for adaptive quantum subspaces
abstract: Quantum subspace methods are often compared by basis dimension or energyerror, although their dominant experimental costs arise from different statepreparations, measurement settings, and shot allocations. We present theDyadic Adaptive Clifford-Algebra Subspace Eigensolver (DA-CASE), whose basisstates are virtual directions $A_i|ψ\rangle$ generated from one reference.Overlap, Hamiltonian, and observable matrices are reconstructed from onecached set of Pauli expectations on that reference. The method thereforetrades multiple prepared basis states for a potentially wide measurement bank.We make that trade explicit on a frozen eight-qubit H$_4$ Hamiltonian. Twogenerator resolutions reach the same nine-dimensional subspace and the sameenergy to machine precision, while the retained bank changes from 7371 to 2240Pauli words. A reference-conditioned symmetry test certifies the narrower spanwithout asserting that its individual Pauli words conserve the sector asabstract operators. Independently, a dyadic commuting hierarchy reduces thedeterminant bank from 913 qubit-wise-commuting settings to 64 fully commutingsettings, while exposing the added logical-CX cost. In a separate four-qubitfinite-shot diagnostic, covariance-aware allocation reduces theprojected-matrix variance target by 68.9%. Mode-wise overlap regularizationremoves the observed catastrophic energy estimates and lowers RMSE, butdoubles the median error relative to a fixed cutoff. These are small-instanceexact and Monte Carlo results, not a hardware demonstration, scaling result,or quantum advantage claim. The contribution is a single-referencemeasurement architecture and a resource ledger that keeps contexts, settings,shots, circuit depth, and post-selection retries in their proper units.
summary: This paper introduces DA-CASE, an efficient measurement architecture that calculates quantum subspaces using only measurements from a single reference state. It demonstrates this by showing that fewer Pauli words are needed to achieve the same accuracy on $	ext{H}_4$ compared to previous methods. The work provides a detailed resource ledger for benchmarking different simulation techniques.
main_problem: The core challenge is efficiently diagonalizing quantum subspaces by managing the measurement overhead associated with finite-shot measurements, which can amplify errors near the null space of the basis matrix.
main_result: The DA-CASE method demonstrates that using a single reference state allows for reconstructing necessary matrices from one cached set of Pauli expectations, significantly reducing the required measurement bank size compared to methods requiring multiple prepared basis states.
method: DA-CASE (Dyadic Adaptive Clifford-Algebra Subspace Eigensolver) reconstructs overlap, Hamiltonian, and observable matrices using only Pauli expectation values measured on a single reference state $|\psiangle$. It employs techniques like dyadic commuting hierarchies and covariance-aware shot allocation to optimize resource usage.
model_or_system: The method is tested primarily on the frozen eight-qubit H4 Hamiltonian ($	ext{H}_4$), with auxiliary tests covering molecular systems like $	ext{H}_2$, LiH, stretched $	ext{H}_4$, and $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$ active spaces.
key_observables: Subspace energy eigenvalues ($E$), Pauli expectation values ($	ext{Tr}(ho \mathbf{A}_i^\dagger \mathbf{A}_j)$), retained Pauli word count (e.g., 7371 vs 2240), projected-matrix variance, and RMSE.
important_parameters: Number of qubits (up to eight), number of basis states/generators, measurement settings ($G$), shot allocations, and context counts ($	ext{Ctx.}$)
main_assumptions: The reported results are small-instance exact and Monte Carlo diagnostics; the authors explicitly state this is not a hardware demonstration or quantum advantage claim.
figures_summary: The notes reference comparisons in Tables I and II showing resource usage across different methods (ADAPT-VQE vs DA-CASE) for H4, and Table III comparing allocation rules on the TFIM bank regarding RMSE and variance reduction.
paper_structure: The paper introduces DA-CASE as a single-reference measurement architecture. It details its components: matrix reconstruction from cached Pauli expectations, adaptive growth using pencil evaluation, symmetry testing, and resource optimization via dyadic grouping and covariance-aware shot allocation. Results are presented by comparing performance metrics across various resolutions on $	ext{H}_4$.
why_interesting: For AMO physicists working on molecular dynamics or quantum chemistry simulations, this work offers a rigorous framework for auditing the computational resources required to achieve high accuracy in variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) type calculations. The explicit resource ledger is highly valuable.
